title: Beehive Temperature and Colony Health
dataSources: Beehive telemetry (`beehive:reading`), coop door (`chickencoop:door`), egg counts (`egg:count`), livestock tags (`livestock:tag`), feed level (`feed:level`), pasture sensors (`pasture:sensor`).
app: Homestead sensors — connected beehive scale/temperature/sound, automatic chicken-coop door, egg counter, livestock GPS/health tags, feed-silo level, and pasture soil sensors — streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT and LoRaWAN gateways.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=beehive:reading
| timechart span=30m avg(brood_temp_c) as brood
| eval unhealthy=if(brood<33 OR brood>36,1,0)
description: Trends the brood-nest temperature bees work hard to keep steady, where a drift signals a struggling or queenless colony.
value: A healthy colony holds brood temperature in a tight band; a persistent drift is an early, non-invasive sign something is wrong.
implementation: Ingest brood-nest temperature into `index=personal`; alert when it drifts outside the healthy band.
visualization: Time chart of brood temperature with a healthy band.
grandmaExplanation: It watches the temperature inside the hive, which healthy bees keep very steady, warning if something is wrong.
